sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Beaumont, TX?
sections.html:
Jefferson County bills it. The Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector collects for the County, the City of Beaumont, Beaumont Independent School District and the other units that tax Beaumont parcels, and the Jefferson Central Appraisal District sets the values those bills are based on.

The Comptroller's county directory shows how many layers can sit on one Beaumont bill. Besides the county, city and school district, it lists the Port of Beaumont Authority, the Sabine-Neches Navigation District, Jefferson County drainage districts, emergency services districts and water control districts. Which of those apply depends on the address.

Jefferson County offices that handle a Beaumont tax account

The tax office posted a notice that the first mailing of 2026 tax bills went out on October 23, 2026. If a bill never reached you, ask the office for a copy.

sections.h2: What is the Beaumont property tax rate?
sections.html:
The council adopts the city rate each fall. On September 14, 2026 the city posted a notice titled "Notice for Meeting to Vote on Tax Rate," along with a notice about its 2026 rates that describes two rates used in adopting the year's rate. The finance department can give you the adopted figure for your account.

The city rate is only one slice. Your total depends on the county, Beaumont ISD and any special district, and each of them adopts its own rate each fall. Texas requires the assessor to mail bills in October, and payment is due on receipt.

  • Look up your account on the Jefferson County tax office site to see the amount each unit levies on your parcel.
  • Compare the line for the City of Beaumont with the line for Beaumont ISD.
  • Check each special district line, which can vary from block to block.

The school line shrinks with a homestead exemption, which is why filing for it matters most for an owner-occupied house.

sections.h2: How do Beaumont homestead and over-65 exemptions work?
sections.html:
Living in the house on January 1 qualifies an owner for a $140,000 school district homestead exemption. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, get $60,000 more off the school bill, and their school tax is held at the level first qualified for. A surviving spouse who is at least 55 may keep the benefit in some cases.

Jefferson CAD's own web page warns about companies that mail a designation-of-homestead form and charge a fee to file an application that costs nothing. You can file directly with the district, even for earlier years in some cases.

Some further points apply to veterans, buyers and heirs.

  • Disabled veterans get exemptions of $5,000 to $12,000 by disability rating, and 100 percent disabled veterans can qualify for a total exemption on their homestead.
  • A buyer closing after January 1 can claim the exemption immediately if the seller never had one.
  • Heirs missing from the recorded deed submit an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a current utility bill.

Most exemption applications are due before May 1.

sections.h2: When are Beaumont property taxes due, and what are the penalties?
sections.html:
Taxes are due on receipt of the October bill and become delinquent if unpaid after January 31. February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest; the penalty then adds a point each month, reaching 12 percent on July 1.

The Jefferson County tax office posts sheriff's sale announcements on its home page, so owners far behind can see how sales are advertised. Units that contract with a collection attorney may tack on up to 20 percent for accounts open on July 1. Older, disabled and disabled veteran owners can pay a homestead bill in four installments; some collectors also offer longer plans on a homestead.

Texas allows a tax unit to sue for unpaid taxes, add court costs to the bill, and ask a court to foreclose. After a tax sale, a homestead owner has two years from the purchaser's deed filing to redeem, with a 25 percent premium the first year and 50 percent the second.

sections.h2: How do I protest a Beaumont appraisal?
sections.html:
A protest to Jefferson CAD is due by May 15, or 30 days after your value notice is delivered when that is later. Homestead notices are mailed about April 1 and notices for other property about May 1.

Open the notice first: it lists the market value, the exemptions on file and the deadline for your account. Grounds worth raising include a value that assumes repairs nobody has made, storm or flood damage, and a nearby sale below the district's number. Bring photos, repair estimates and comparable sales.

After the appraisal review board rules, you can appeal to district court, choose binding arbitration, or take a value over $1,000,000 to the State Office of Administrative Hearings. A homestead cap holds assessed value to 10 percent growth a year, but only starting the year after the exemption is first granted.

sections.h2: What does the Beaumont housing market look like?
sections.html:
Census counts for Beaumont run downward: 118,296 in 2010, 115,282 in 2020, and an estimated 112,967 in July 2025, which is 1.8 percent under the 2020 base. The city covers 82.47 land square miles at 1,397.9 people per square mile.

About 55.3 percent of homes are owner occupied. The 2020 to 2024 survey gives a $166,400 median home value, $1,121 median rent and $1,698 monthly owner cost with a mortgage. Median household income is $56,997 and 21.2 percent of people live in poverty. The city counts 45,001 households and 6,493 veterans, and the typical commute is 20.3 minutes.

Retail sales were $3,248,844 thousand in 2022 and health care and social assistance receipts reached $1,682,045 thousand. For a seller who owes back taxes, exact payoff figures from the county tax office are the first thing to collect. An heir who inherited a Beaumont house should also ask Jefferson CAD whether the prior owner's homestead exemption was carried forward.

sections.h2: What should a Beaumont seller bring to a closing when taxes are owed?
sections.html:
Start with the tax office's account page, which shows each year's balance. The tax lien arises each January 1, which means a title company will not clear the house until every open year, with penalties and interest, is paid.

  • A payoff figure good through the closing date, because penalty and interest accrue monthly.
  • Proof of any homestead, over-65, disability or veteran exemption, so the buyer's escrow is not short.
  • Any installment agreement paperwork, if the account is on a plan.
  • Letters testamentary or an affidavit of heirship for an inherited house.

Liability for a given year's tax stays with whoever held title on January 1, so the settlement statement should spell out which side pays which share.

faqs.q: Which office do I pay Beaumont property taxes to?
faqs.a: The Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector, at 1149 Pearl St., Beaumont, phone 409-835-8516. The county collects for the city, Beaumont ISD and other units on your bill.

faqs.q: When did Beaumont 2026 tax bills go out?
faqs.a: The Jefferson County tax office announced on October 23, 2026 that the first mailing of 2026 bills was in the mail. State law has the assessor mail bills around October 1, and they are due on receipt.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Beaumont taxes late?
faqs.a: On February 1 a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach, and penalty rises 1 percent a month to 12 percent on July 1. Attorney fees can add up to 20 percent.

faqs.q: How do I get a homestead exemption in Beaumont?
faqs.a: Apply with the Jefferson Central Appraisal District, which takes homestead applications directly at no cost. The house must be yours and your principal residence, and you cannot claim a second homestead elsewhere.

faqs.q: Does the Beaumont city rate apply to my whole bill?
faqs.a: No. It is one line. Jefferson County, Beaumont ISD and any special district each add their own rate, and your bill shows all of them together.
